data.title: Solving a Linear Equation with Subtraction and Division
data.subject: Algebra

problem.statement: Solve the linear equation $3x - 7 = 14$ for $x$. State your final answer in simplest form.

data.solutionStrategy: Isolate the variable term by applying inverse operations in reverse order of operations.

steps.title: Isolate the variable term by adding 7 to both sides
steps.strategy: Addition undoes subtraction, allowing us to gather all constant terms on the right side of the equation.
steps.misconceptions: Adding 7 only to the left side or incorrectly subtracting 7 instead of adding.

steps.title: Isolate the variable by dividing both sides by 3
steps.strategy: Division undoes multiplication, which successfully isolates the variable completely.
steps.misconceptions: Dividing only the coefficient or dividing the constant by the wrong number.

data.gradeLevel: middle school students (grades 6-8) - Use more complex vocabulary, abstract concepts, real-world applications, and critical thinking opportunities. Encourage deeper analysis.
